Barua huandikwa katika karatasi na kutiwa katika bahasha na kisha kutumwa kwa aliyelengwa kupokea barua hiyo.
Hata hivyo, kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia hivi sasa barua huandikwa kama ujumbe katika simu na kisha kutumwa kwa mlengwa na kumfikia mara moja.
Hii haimanishi kuwa mfumo za zamani wa kuandika na kutumiana barua haupo ila inakidhi kusema kuwa umepungua kasi kutokana na maijilio ya sayansi na teknolojia na kuonekana kuwa barua za kuandika katika karatasi na kutumwa kwa mlengwa hutumia muda mrefu kumfikia mhusika (Khamis, 2007).
Utumaji wa barua kwa njia ya simu na mtandao kama barua pepe unafanya barua kutumia muda wa kufumba na kufumbua macho kumfikia mlengwa.
Yote kwa yote lakini ni ukweli kuwa bado matumizi ya barua kama chombo cha mawasiliano katika jamii.

Riwaya ya Kiswahili Riwaya ya Kiswahili ni moja kati ya tanzu nne za fasihi andishi ya Kiswahili huku nyingine zikiwa ni tamthiliya, ushairi na hadithi fupi (Wamitila, 2008).
Utanzu wa riwaya ndio unaotumika kueleza mambo kwa kina na mapana zaidi kuliko tanzu nyingine za fasihi andishi.
Kutokana na hali hii, riwaya huwasilisha dhamira za kisiasa, kijamii na kiutamaduni kwa jamii kwa kutumia visa na matukio yaelezwayo katika riwaya husika.
Mohamed Suleiman ni mmoja kati ya watunzi wa riwaya za Kiswahili ambaye anatunga visa na matukio mbalimbali yatoayo dhamira zenye mashiko kwa jamii.

Riwaya ya Kiu Kiu ni riwaya ya Kiswahili inayoelezea hadithi ya Bahati, kijana mwanamke aliyelelewa akaleleka na sasa anakutana na Idi, mwanaume laghai.

Kama ndege aliyenaswa katika ulimbo, jitihada zake za kujipatia nusura zinamletea angamio.
Riwaya ya Kiu ilipata zawadi ya kwanza katika mashindano ya uandishi wa hadithi za kubuni katika lugha ya Kiswahili, ambayo yaliandaliwa mnamo mwaka 1970.

Fani ni nini?
Fani ni ufundi wa kisanaa unaotumiwa na mwandishi anapoandika au kusimulia kazi yake ya fasihi mbele ya hadhira aliyoiteua kwa ajili ya kazi hiyo.
Fani hujumuisha vipengele vya matumizi ya lugha, muundo, mtindo, wahusika na mandhari.
Vipengele hivi kwa umoja wake ndivyo vinavyomwezesha mwandishi wa kazi ya fasihi kujenga dhamira na mawazo yake na kuyawasilisha kwa hadhira iliyolengwa.
Matumizi ya vipengele vya fani hutofautiana na wakati mwingine hata kufanana baina ya mwandishi mmoja na mwingine.
Mohamed Suleiman katika riwaya ya Kiu ametumia mbinu mbalimbali za kifani ili kuwasilisha dhamira kwa hadhira iliyokusudiwa lakini katika kazi hii hatuwezi kushughulikia mbinu zote.
Baadhi ya mbinu za kisanaa tulizozitafiti katika kazi hii ni mbinu ya matumizi ya barua, taharuki, misemo, sitiari na tashihisi.
Fani ni ule ufundi wa kisanaa unaotumiwa na mwandishi kuisana kazi yake ili wasomaji na wasikilizaji waweze kuifurahia (Njogu na Chimerah, 1999).

5.1 Mbinu za Kifani katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili
5.1.1 Matumizi ya Mbinu ya Barua Barua ni njia kongwe ya mawasiliano baina ya mtu na mtu, mtu na watu, taasisi na mtu, taasisi na taasisi inayolenga kutoa taarifa au ujumbe fulani ambao ni muhimu kufahamika kwa upande uliolengwa
Iddi alipokea barua kwa mshangao maana hakuwa akiitazamia.
Aliigeuza upande wa pili, akaona jina la Bahati limeandikwa kwa mkono uliokuwa wa haraka.
Akaifungua na kusoma: Iddi, Usistaajabu nikikuambia ya kuwa hivi sasa niko kitandani kwa bwana Mwinyi, tunapanga siku ya arusi yetu ya kikweli.
Si ruhusa kutuingilia kwani tuna hiari yetu.
Nakuonya kwa salama yako mwenyewe, kuwa mipango yako iwe imekoma baada ya kuipata barua hii.
Nisalimie fulani … Wa nafsi yangu, Bahati.
Barua ile iliwasha moto moyoni mwa Iddi na kumchemsha kwa hasira.
Ilimwia kama dhoruba kali ya ghafla.
Mara macho yake yaligeuka rangi, kipaji kikapetana, na kidevu kikamwanguka, kwa ajabu ya uchungu.
Aliisoma tena ile barua, na kila alipozidi kuisoma ndivyo alivyozidi kuchafuka kwa hasira (uk.
58-59).
Barua hii iliandikwa na bahati kwenda kwa Iddi ambaye ni mpenzi wake ambaye anampenda sana lakini hapa anamtaarifu kuwa sasa yeye amekwishakuwa na mapenzi na mtu mwingine aitwaye Mwinyi.
Mwinyi ni bosi wa Iddi na Iddi alimtaka Bahati kumrubuni Mwinyi kuwa anampenda ili wapate fedha lakini anayependwa kwa dhati ni Iddi.
Sasa ni jambo la kushtusha sana kuona mapenzi ya Mwinyi na Bahati yanakuwa ni ya kweli na si mzaha kama Iddi alivyotaraji.
Iddi sasa anaingiwa na mashaka makubwa kama kweli utajiri alioutaka kutoka kwa Mwinyi kupitia kwa Bahati ataupata au ndio umeshapotea.
Dhamira ya mapenzi na ile ya wizi na magendo zinakuzwa kwa kiasi kikubwa kutokana na matumizi ya barua iliyopo hapo juu.
Bahati anapima kama kweli Iddi anampenda kwa dhati naye Iddi anapata hasira kuwa mradi wake wa kutaka kupata utajiri wa Mwinyi kupitia kwa bahati unapotea.
Pia, kupitia barua iliyopo hapo juu mwandishi anajenga dhamira kuwa si kila jambo linaweza kuwa kama vile mtu alivyotaraji liwe.
Mipango na utekelezaji wa jambo ni vitu viwili tofauti ingawa vinategemeana (Scott, 1995).
Iddi hakutegemea kuwa kumwambia Bahati ajidai kuwa anampenda Mwinyi ili wapate utajiri kunaweza kumfanya Bahati akampenda Mwinyi Kikweli kweli na kumuacha yeye.
Hapa panajengwa dhamira ya maonyo kwamba mapenzi huwa hayajaribishwi kwani wakati na saa yoyote yanaweza kubadilika na kuwa tofauti kabisa na ilivyokusudiwa.

5.1.2 Matumizi ya Misemo katika Kiu Misemo ni kauli zinazokaribiana na kushahabiana na methali itumiwayo na wanadamu kama chombo cha mawasiliano (Msokile, 1992).
Hata hivyo, mara nyingi misemo huwa haina pande mbili kama ilivyo kwa methali.
Methali kwa upande wake huwa na pande mbili ambapo upende mmoja huwa ni kama swali na upande wa pili huwa ndio jibu la swali lililoulizwa (Wamitila, 2003).
Misemo ni kauli ambazo hutokana na misimu ambayo kanuni yake ni kuwa huibuka na kupotea na ile ambayo haipotei inadumu ndio huitwa misemo.
Misemo ni mbinu ya kifani inayotumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi ili kukazia au kutoa msisitizo juu ya dhamira fulani ambayo wanataka hadhira yao ipate.
Mohamed Suleimani katika riwaya yake ya Kiu ametumia misemo katika kazi yake hii kama ifuatavyo:
Iddi hayakuwa mazuri kwake kwani lengo la Iddi halikuwa ni la kumpenda kwa dhati bali kumchezea tu.
Wazazi waliuo wengi wanafahamu kuwa, vijana wanapokuwa na mahusiano ya kimapenzi kabla ndoa mara nyingi huishia kuchezeana na suala la kuoana hupotea.
Hivyo, kama mzazi Cheusi alimtaka binti yake aachane mara moja na Iddi.
Msemo uliotumika katika kifungu hapo juu umetumika kujenga na kutoa msisitizo wa dhamira ya malezi ya mama kwa mto wake.
Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kuwa mazoe ni kitu kinachojenga tabia na daima mazoea huendelea daima (Ritzer, 2008).
Kama katika jamii wasichana na wavulana wanaachwa huru kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa watalifanya hilo kuwa ni jambo sahihi na suala la kufunga ndoa halitakuwa na umuhimu kwao tena.
Ni lazima wazazi wafanye kazi yao vizuri ili wanajamii hasa vijana waone kwamba kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa ni kitu kibaya na hakifai kuenziwa hata mara moja.
5.1.3 Matumizi ya Sitiari katika Kiu Sitiari ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika katika kulinganisha vitu viwili vyenye sifa tofauti bila ya kutumia kiunganishi vya kufananisha kama ilivyo katika tashibiha (Kyando, 2013).
Vitu vinavyolinganishwa huchukuliwa kuwa ni sawa sawa kabisa na havina tofauti yoyote ile.
Kwa mfano, mtu anaweza akasema “Mwajuma ni sungura mdogo aliyejificha juu ya mti.” Hapa Mwajuma anafananishwa na sungura kana kwamba ni vitu viwili vilivyo sawa sawa bila ya tofauti hata kidogo.
Lengo hasa la kutumia sitiari katika kazi za fasihi ni kutoa msisitizo juu ya dhamira inayowasilishwa kwa msomaji.
Mohamed Suleiman ametumia sitiari pale aliposema:
Watu waliposema kuwa hakuna aliyepata kumwia Mwinyi, maneno yao hayakuwa yametiwa chumvi.
Mwinyi alikuwa na fedha za kutosha kujinunulia vingi ya vile mzee wa miaka sitini na miwili kama yeye angevitamani isipokuwa kitu kimoja tu.
Hicho ndicho kilichomfanya hata akaona kama kwamba umri wake wote alioishi umepotea bure, na ule utajiri wake mfano wa kitumbua kilichotiwa mchanga (uk.01).
Maneno yaliyokolezwa wino katika kifungu cha maneno hapo huu ni msemo unaoashira kuwa jambo au kitu kizuri sasa kimekuwa kibaya, kitu kitamu sasa kimekuwa kichungu na kitu cha thamani sasa thamani yake imepotea.
Mzee Mwinyi alikuwa ni tajiri mwenye kila aina ya mali lakini alitamani kuwa na mapenzi na binti aliyetokea kumpenda sana akiitwa Bahati.
Kila mbinu aliyoitumia haikufanikiwa katika kumfanya Mwinyi ampate Bahati ndipo hata akalalamika kuwa, “utajiri wake mfano wa kitumbua kilichotiwa mchanga,” kwamba utajiri wake haumsaidii na wala hauna faida yoyote ile kwake.
Kimsingi, kitumbua ambacho kinakuwa kimetiwa mchanga huwa hakiliki na ladha yake yote hupotea kwa sababu mlaji huogopa meno yake kutafuna mchanga.
Msemo huu kwa hakika umetumika katika kutoa msisitizo wa dhamira ya mapenzi kuwa ikiwa mtu ni tajiri wa kila kitu lakini anapokosa mapenzi aliyoyatamani basi utajiri wake huwa si lolote na humfanya aishi kwa taabu na adha ya mawazo kiliko hata mtu maskini.
Wanasosholojia wanakiri kwamba vipo baadhi ya vitu ambavyo huonekana ni bora sana mtu kuwa navyo mathalani utajiri (Cross, 2011).
Lakini hufika mahali mtu akakosa kitu ambacho alidhani kuwa ni kidogo na ule utajiri wake usimsaidie katika kukipata kitu hicho hali yeye aliamini kuwa utajiri wake ndio silaha ya kupata kila kitu.
Hii ni sawa na kusema kuwa, sasa kitumbua kimeingia mchanga kwani utajiri wote wa Mwinyi haukumwezesha kupata mapenzi ya Bahati.
Matumizi mengine ya msemo yanajitokeza pale ambapo Cheusi ambaye ni mama yake Bahati alipokuwa akimuonya mwanawe juu ya mahusiano yake na Iddi.
Anasema:
Palikuwa na kimya kifupi lakini kichungu.
Halafu Cheusi akazidi kumshauri: “Huyo Iddi wako huyo, nikwambie, hana kukutaka, hana chochote.
Anayemtaka mwanamke humuoa.
Yeye anataka akuchezee na halafu akutupilie mbali, apite akikucheka.
Nimekwishatambua kama wewe umesoma hicho Kizungu chako unaniona mimi mjinga basi haya … Utakuja lia kilio cha mbwa mdomo juu, mimi niko hapa (uk.
25-26).” Katika kifungu hiki cha maneno mwandishi anatumia msemo, “utakuja lia kilio cha mbwa mdomo juu,” kurejelea dhamira ya malezi na maonyo yanayotolewa na mama kwa mwanaye.
Cheusi alikuwa akimuonya mwanaye Bahati kuwa mahusiano yake aliyoanzisha na
Pende hivi, Iddi, dereva wake aliingia bila ya kubisha hodi.
Mwinyi alishtuka na kumuuliza, “mbona umekawia?” Iddi alifuta jasho kuonesha jitihadi aliyofanya, akatikisa kichwa kwa masikitiko na kusema, “nimekuta kufuli mlangoni.” Maneno yale yalimkata Mwinyi ini lake.
Alishusha mabega akanywea juu ya kiti, akaona maisha yakimwonea.
Kusubiri kusiko kikomo- miezi sita imepita na kutamani kusiko danganyika kukimtwesha.
Alikuwa amekwishavumilia vya kutosha; bado hakujua ni lini siku ya faraja.
Lakini ah, maneno ya marehemu mama yake: Likufikalo patana nalo (uk.02).
Matumizi ya sitiari katika kifungu cha maneno hapo juu yanabainisha kuwa maneno yamefafanishwa na kisu au kitu chochote ambacho ni kikali chenye uwezo wa kukata kitu.
“Maneno yale yalimkata Mwinyi ini lake,” ni kauli yenye kuonesha kuwa matumaini ya Mwinyi kumpata Bahati yalikwishapotea mara baada ya taarifa kutoka kwa Iddi kuwa amemkosa Bahati na mlango wa nyumba ya Bahati umefungwa.
Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kuwa mwanadamu hufika mahali akakata tamaa juu ya kupata kitu fulani ambacho alitaraji kukipata kwa muda mrefu na asikipate (Webster, 2006).
Kukata tamaa katika maisha ni jambo baya kwani huweza kumfanya mtu akafanya jambo baya ambalo hata linaweza kudhuru watu wengine.
Kwa mfano, kitendo cha Mwinyi kukata tamaa ya kumpata Bahati kinaweza kikamfanya Mwinyi kuja na maamuzi ya kufanya uhalifu wa kubaka.
Kitendo cha ubakaji ni kibaya kwa ambaye atakuwa amebakwa lakini pia kwa mbakaji kwani huweza kuishia jela katika maisha yake yote yaliyobakia.
Mzee wa miaka sitini na miwili kama Mwinyi kufungwa jela ni kitu kibaya ambacho kinaweza kumfanya akafia huko jela.

Hata hivyo inaelezwa kuwa kitu chenyewe kilikuwa ni hari ya mtu tena mtu huyo ana kiburi na maringo.
Maelezo haya yanaonyesha kuwa kitu hicho hakikutajwa kuwa ni kitu gani jambo ambalo linamfanya msomaji aliye makini kutaka kujua kulikoni hata jambo hilo likamshughulisha Mwinyi kiasi hicho?
Matumizi hayo ya taharuki yatamfanya msomaji aendelee kusoma riwaya ya Kiu mpaka pale atakapolifahamu hilo jambo ambalo linamsumbua Mwinyi.
Kadri anavyoendelea kusoma ndipo anapokutana na maneno haya:
Tashihisi ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika katika kuvipa urari na uwezo wa kutenda kama binadamu viumbe au vitu ambavyo havina uwezo huo (Mlacha, 1989).
Vitu kama vile miti, maneno, wadudu, wanyama na ndege wanaosawiriwa wakifanya vitendo vya kibinadamu hali ya kuwa hawana uwezo wa kufanya vitendo hivyo.
Kwa mfano, si jambo la ajabu kuona katika fasihi ndege wakichumbiana na kupeleka posa la kuoa na hatimaye ndoa hufungwa na ndege hao wakaishi raha mustarehe (Senkoro, 2006).
Matumizi ya tashihisi katika kazi za fasihi hufanywa kwa lengo la kujenga dhamira kitaswira ili kumfanya msomaji atafakari kidogo ndipo aweze kupata dhamira iliyokusudiwa na mwandishi au msimuliaji wa kazi iliyo mbele yake.
Katika riwaya ya Kiu kuna matumizi ya tashihisi yaliyotumiwa kwa lengo kama hilo ambayo yanajitokeza kama ifuatavyo:
“Ati watu husema mapenzi hayakutani, mbona yako wewe na Bahati yamekutana?”
Bahati alilia kwa kite na simanzi, hata usingizi ukamuonea huruma, ukamchukua hima na kumpumzisha kitandani.
Alizindushwa na vishindo vya waenda msikitini, maana tayari kulikwisha pambazuka.
Saa ya Bahati, siku zote ilikuwa wapiti njia.
Alikuwa amekwishazoea kusikia wakati wa nyendo za wale waendao kazini, shule, misikitini, ndege za abiria, na waadhini (uk.20).
Maneno yaliyokolezwa wino katika kifungu cha maneno hapo juu yametumiwa kitashihisi kwani katika maisha halisi ni mwanadamu pekee ndiye mwenye urari wa kuwa na huruma kwa mtu au kiumbe mwingine yoyote.
Usingizi ni hali ya mtu kulala akawa hana fahamu kwani Waswahili husema, “usingizi ni nusu ya kufa.” Hata hivyo, katika kifungu cha maneno hapo juu inaonekana kuwa usingizi umepewa uwezo wa kuwa na huruma kama mwanadamu.
5.1.5 Matumizi ya Taharuki katika Kiu Taharuki ni mbinu ya kifani inayotumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi katika kuzisana kazi zao hata zikafikisha dhamira zilizokusudiwa kwa hadhira iliyolengwa.
Hii ni mbinu ya kumchelewesha msomaji katika kupata suluhisho au ukweli wa mambo ulivyo na kumfanya aendelee kusoma zaidi mpaka pale atakapokutana na suluhisho au maelezo fulani yatakayompatia jawabu alilokusudia kulipata (Senkoro, 2006).
Mbinu ya taharuki hutumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi kwa makusudi mazima ya kumpatia msomaji au msikilizaji hamu ya kusoma hasa kazi husika inapokuwa ni ndefu kiasi cha kumchosha msomaji.
Urefu wa kazi utaonekana kuwa ni mfupi sana kama kutakuwa na taharuki zenye kumvutia msomaji.
Taharuki ni mbinu kongwe ya kifani inayotumika sana katika fasihi simulizi na hata katika fasihi andishi.
Mohamed Suleiman katika riwaya yake ya Kiu ametumia mbinu hii kwa namna alivyoanza kusimulia hadithi yake.
Kwa mfano:
Jioni hiyo alikuwa amejinyoosha juu ya kiti cha kulala, macho yake kayatupa darini, akihesabu dakika.
Tamaa yake haikuwa kubwa, na wasiwasi wa kutofaulu ulimwondolea furaha.

Keywords: Novel, Written Literature, Technical Techniques, Style, Literature

A B S T R A C T
A work of literature, including a novel, is formed by technique and content, which together constitute what we refer to as literature. Technique is composed of elements such as characters, style, setting, structure, and the use of language. These elements are utilized by writers in various ways depending on their skills and abilities. In terms of technique, it refers to the overall main ideas expressed by the author or narrator of the literary work and intended for the audience to receive. This work was intended to investigate the various themes presented by Mohamed Suleiman in his Swahili novel "Kiu." Through this novel, we have identified and discussed the literary techniques used by the author to bring out the themes within the novel. 'Kiu' is a Swahili novel that tells the story of Bahati, a young woman who was raised with care and is now encountering Idi, a deceitful man. Idi quickly entangles Bahati in the trap of false love. While Bahati is deeply immersed in love, unaware of herself and her surroundings, she realizes that Idi does not truly love her, but instead loves only himself, and that she, Bahati, is merely an instrument to fulfill his worldly desires. Like a bird caught in a snare, her efforts to find escape only lead her closer to ruin. Introduction

3. The Swahili novel is one of the four genres of written Swahili literature, the others being drama, poetry, and the short story (Wamitila, 2008). The novel genre is used to explain matters in greater depth and breadth than other genres of written literature. As a result, the novel conveys political, social, and cultural themes to society through the stories and events presented in the specific novel. Mohamed Suleiman is one of the authors of Swahili novels who crafts various stories and events that present substantial themes for society. 4. The novel 'Kiu' is a Swahili novel that tells the story of Bahati, a young woman who was raised with care and is now encountering Idi, a deceitful man. Idi quickly entangles Bahati in the trap of false love. Lost in love and oblivious to herself, Bahati realizes that Idi does not truly love her, but rather loves himself, and that she, Bahati, is merely a tool for fulfilling his worldly desires. Like a bird caught in a trap, her efforts to find escape only bring her ruin. The novel 'Kiu' won first prize in the Kiswahili fiction writing competition, which was organized in 1970. 5. What is technique? Technique is the artistic craftsmanship employed by a writer when composing or narrating their literary work before the specific audience intended for that work. Technique encompasses elements such as use of language, structure, style, characters, and setting. Together, these elements enable the writer of a literary work to construct and convey their themes and ideas to the intended audience. The use of these technical elements varies, and may sometimes even be similar, from one writer to another. Mohamed Suleiman, in the novel 'Kiu', has employed various literary techniques to present the themes to the intended audience; however, in this work, we cannot address all of the techniques. Some of the artistic techniques we have examined in this work include the use of letters, suspense, proverbs, metaphors, and personification. Technique refers to the artistic craftsmanship employed by a writer to craft their work so that readers and listeners can enjoy it (Njogu and Chimerah, 1999). Technique is composed of elements such as characters, style, setting, structure, and use of language. These elements are used by writers in different ways depending on their skill and expertise. (Simiyu, 2011). 5.1 Literary Techniques in the Swahili Novel  
5.1.1 The Use of the Letter Technique  
A letter is an ancient means of communication between an individual and another individual, an individual and a group, an institution and an individual, or between institutions. Its aim is to convey information or a particular message that is important for the intended recipient to know.  
Idi received the letter with surprise because he was not expecting it. He turned the letter over and saw Bahati’s name written in hurried handwriting. He opened it and read:  
Idi,  
Don’t be surprised when I tell you that right now I am in bed with Mr. Mwinyi, and we are planning the day for our real wedding. It is not permitted to interfere with us because we have our own free will. I warn you for your own safety, that your plans should cease once you have received this letter. Send my regards to so-and-so … From the depths of my heart, Bahati. The letter ignited a fire in Idi’s heart and boiled him with anger. It struck him like a sudden, fierce storm. Suddenly his eyes changed color, his forehead became furrowed, and his jaw dropped, in a display of intense anguish. He read that letter again, and the more he read it, the angrier he became. 58-59). This letter was written by Bahati to Idi, her lover whom she loves very much, but here she is informing him that she is now in love with another person named Mwinyi. Mwinyi is Idi's boss, and Idi wanted Bahati to deceive Mwinyi by making him believe she loved him so that they could get money, while in reality, the one she truly loved was Idi. Now, it is truly shocking to see that the love between Mwinyi and Bahati has become genuine and not a joke as Idi had expected. Idi is now filled with great doubt about whether the wealth he hoped to gain from Mwinyi through Bahati will actually materialize, or if it has already been lost. The theme of love, as well as that of theft and smuggling, are greatly developed through the use of the letter mentioned above. Bahati is weighing whether Idi truly loves her, while Idi grows angry as his plan to gain Mwinyi's wealth through Bahati slips away. Also, through the above letter, the author develops the theme that not everything can turn out as one expects. Planning and implementation of something are two different things, although they are interdependent (Scott, 1995). Idi did not expect that telling Bahati to pretend to love Mwinyi so they could gain wealth would actually make Bahati truly fall in love with Mwinyi and leave him. Here, the theme of warnings is developed, emphasizing that love should not be experimented with, as at any moment it can change and become completely different from what was originally intended. Proverbs are expressions that are similar to and resemble sayings used by human beings as tools of communication (Msokile, 1992). However, proverbs often do not have two sides as is the case with sayings. A proverb, on its part, has two sides, where one side serves as a question and the other side provides the answer to the question posed (Wamitila, 2003). Proverbs are sayings that arise from expressions whose nature is that they emerge and disappear, and those that do not disappear but endure are what are called proverbs. Proverbs are a literary technique used by authors of literary works to underscore or emphasize a particular theme they want their audience to grasp. In his novel *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman has used proverbs in his work as follows: Things were not good for Idi, as his intention was not to truly love her but merely to toy with her. Most responsible parents know that when young people engage in romantic relationships before marriage, it often leads to them toying with each other and the issue of marriage gets lost. Therefore, as a parent, Cheusi wanted her daughter to end things with Idi immediately. The proverb used in the above passage has been employed to build and emphasize the theme of a mother's guidance to her child. Sociologists explain that habit is something that shapes character, and habits always persist (Ritzer, 2008). If in society girls and boys are left free to have relationships before marriage, they will consider it acceptable, and the issue of getting married will no longer hold any significance for them. Parents must fulfill their responsibilities properly so that members of society, especially the youth, see that having relationships before marriage is a bad thing that should never be encouraged. 5.1.3 The Use of Metaphor in Kiu

A metaphor is a figure of speech that is used to compare two things with different characteristics without using any linking word of comparison, as is the case with simile (Kyando, 2013). The things being compared are considered to be entirely alike, without any differences. For example, one might say, “Mwajuma is a little rabbit hiding in a tree.” Here, Mwajuma is being compared to a rabbit as if they are two things that are exactly alike, without any difference at all. The main purpose of using metaphors in literary works is to emphasize the theme being presented to the reader. Mohamed Suleiman used a metaphor when he said:  
When people said that no one had ever outsmarted Mwinyi, their words were not exaggerated. Mwinyi had enough money to buy himself most of the things that a sixty-two-year-old man like him could desire, except for just one thing. That is what made him feel as though his entire life had been wasted, and that his wealth was like a rice cake that had been spoiled with sand (p.01). The words emphasized in ink in the phrase here express a saying that something good has now turned bad, something sweet has now become bitter, and something valuable has now lost its value. Mr. Mwinyi was a wealthy man who possessed all kinds of riches, but he longed to have a romantic relationship with a young woman named Bahati, whom he had come to love deeply. Every approach he tried failed to win Bahati over, leading him to complain that “his wealth was like a cake mixed with sand,” meaning his wealth did not help him at all and was of no benefit to him. Essentially, a rice cake that has sand mixed into it becomes inedible and loses all its flavor because the eater fears their teeth will bite into the sand. This saying has indeed been used to emphasize the theme of love—that if a person is wealthy in every material sense but lacks the love they long for, then their wealth becomes meaningless and causes them to live with more hardship and mental anguish than even a poor person. Sociologists acknowledge that there are certain things which are generally considered highly desirable to possess, such as wealth (Cross, 2011). However, there comes a time when a person lacks something they thought was minor, and their wealth does not help them obtain it, even though they believed their riches were the key to getting everything. This is akin to saying that the rice cake now has sand in it, for all of Mwinyi’s wealth could not enable him to win Bahati’s love. Another use of the saying appears when Cheusi, who is Bahati’s mother, was warning her daughter about her relationship with Idi. He says:
There was a brief but bitter silence. Then Cheusi continued to advise her: "That Idi of yours, let me tell you, he doesn't want you, he has nothing. Whoever truly desires a woman marries her. He just wants to toy with you and then discard you, moving on while laughing at you. I have already realized that just because you have studied your English you think I am ignorant, well then … One day you will cry like a dog, mouth raised, and I will be here (pp. 25–26).” In this passage the writer uses the saying, “you will cry like a dog, mouth raised,” to refer to the theme of guidance and warnings given by a mother to her child. Cheusi was warning her daughter Bahati about the relationship she had started with
At that moment, Iddi, her driver, entered without knocking. Mwinyi was startled and asked him, “Why are you late?” Iddi wiped his sweat to show the effort he had made, shook his head sadly, and said, “I found the door locked.” Those words broke Mwinyi’s heart. He slumped his shoulders and shrank into the chair, feeling that life was being unfair to him. Waiting without end—six months had passed, and relentless yearning weighed heavily upon him. He had already endured enough; yet he still did not know when the day of relief would come. But ah, her late mother’s words: “Whatever comes your way, accept it” (p. 02). The use of metaphor in the above phrase shows that words are compared to a knife or anything sharp that is capable of cutting something. “Those words struck Mwinyi to the core,” is a statement that shows Mwinyi’s hope of winning Bahati had vanished as soon as he received information from Idi that he could not find Bahati and that Bahati’s door was locked. Sociologists explain that a person may reach a point where they lose hope of obtaining something they have long desired but are unable to acquire (Webster, 2006). Losing hope in life is a bad thing because it can lead a person to do something harmful that may even endanger others. For example, Mwinyi's despair at not being able to have Bahati could drive him to make the decision to commit a crime such as rape. The act of rape is terrible for the victim but also for the perpetrator, as it can result in spending the rest of their life in prison. For a sixty-two-year-old man like Mwinyi to be imprisoned is a terrible thing that could cause him to die in prison. 5.1.4 The Use of Personification

However, it is said that the issue was actually a person’s temperament—and that person is arrogant and boastful. These descriptions show that the thing in question is not specified, which makes the keen reader want to find out what exactly it is that is troubling Mwinyi so much. Personification is a figure of speech used to give balance and the ability to act like humans to creatures or objects that do not possess such abilities (Mlacha, 1989). Things such as trees, words, insects, animals, and birds are depicted as performing human actions even though they do not have the ability to do so. For example, it is not unusual in literature to find birds courting, proposing marriage, and eventually getting married and living happily ever after (Senkoro, 2006). The use of personification in literary works is intended to build the theme in an imaginative way so that the reader reflects a little in order to grasp the intended theme of the author or narrator of the work before them. In the novel *Kiu*, there is the use of personification applied for this very purpose, as manifested in the following excerpt:
“People say that love never meets, but why have yours and Bahati’s?”
Bahati cried out with anguish and sorrow, until even sleep took pity on her, swiftly overtook her, and rested her on the bed. She was awakened by the clamoring of people going to the mosque, for dawn had already broken. Bahati’s sense of time was always guided by passersby. She had become accustomed to hearing the movements of people going to work, to school, to the mosque, passenger airplanes, and the calls to prayer (p.20). The words emphasized in the above passage are used as personification, because in real life only a human being is capable of showing compassion toward another person or creature. Sleep is a state in which a person loses consciousness, as expressed in the Swahili saying, "sleep is half of death." However, in the above passage, sleep appears to have been given the ability to feel compassion, as if it were human. 5.1.5 The Use of Suspense in Kiu

Suspense is a literary technique used by authors of literary works to craft their works in such a way that they effectively convey their intended themes to the target audience. This is a technique of delaying the reader from obtaining the solution or the truth of the matter, and making them continue reading until they encounter a solution or some explanation that will provide the answer they intended to find (Senkoro, 2006). The suspense technique is deliberately used by authors of literary works to give the reader or listener the desire to continue reading, especially when the work in question is lengthy enough to tire the reader. The length of the work will seem very short if there are suspenseful moments that captivate the reader. Suspense is an ancient literary technique that is widely used in oral literature and even in written literature. Mohamed Suleiman, in his novel *Kiu*, has employed this technique in the way he begins narrating his story. For example:

That evening, he was stretched out on a reclining chair, his eyes fixed on the ceiling, counting the minutes. His desire was not great, and the anxiety of failure had robbed him of joy. If only what he wanted was within his grasp, he would seize it and quench his thirst. If what he wanted could be bought with money, he would surely have scraped together every cent he had. But the thing itself depended on the will of another person, someone with taste and pride. So he had no choice but to ask and wait (pp. 01–02). This passage contains a sense of anxiety, as there is something that makes Mwinyi uncomfortable and torments him despite being wealthy. This is not stated explicitly, but it is merely mentioned that if obtaining that thing required money, Mwinyi would provide it.  
“Stop joking, Iddi,” Mwinyi scolded him. “Do you think a child like that could love an old man like me (p.05)?” In this passage, the tension built by the author on the first page of his novel begins to find answers on page five. This is where the issue that troubles Mwinyi is mentioned, to the extent that he lacks peace despite all his great wealth. That thing is none other than the love he had for a girl known by the name Bahati. Mwinyi was a man of sixty-two years, but he loved Bahati very much, even though she was a young girl who had not yet finished school. In this context, another tension arises: could Bahati agree to become the lover of an older man, just as Mwinyi did? This too creates suspense for the readers, who will be compelled to read further to find out what will happen regarding Mwinyi’s love for the young girl Bahati. The use of this technique of suspense has been employed with the aim of enhancing and developing the theme of love in the novel Kiu. This technique appears to be used repeatedly, as whenever the answer or solution to the initial suspense is found, another suspense is introduced (Mlacha, 1991). For example, in the excerpt above we find the solution that what had been troubling Mwinyi Raha and causing him sleepless nights was his love for Bahati's daughter. After realizing this, another anxiety has arisen as to whether such a young girl like Bahati could agree to be in a relationship with old Mwinyi, who could even be Bahati's father. Readers will continue reading until they find a solution, and after that, they will encounter another anxiety. Conclusion The specific objective of this work was to analyze and describe the stylistic techniques used to construct social themes in the novel "Kiu" by Mohamed Suleiman. Accordingly, the findings include the use of stylistic techniques such as letters, expressions, metaphors, personification, and anxiety. The research findings show that the novel 'Kiu' by Mohamed Suleiman is rich in stylistic techniques, but in this study we have focused only on the use of the letter-writing technique, sayings, metaphor, anxiety, and suspense. The main reason for selecting these five techniques is that they adequately meet the objectives of this research. The use of the letter-writing technique was employed with the aim of developing and advancing the theme of love, in which Bahati wanted to know if Iddi truly loved her. Bahati wrote a letter to inform Iddi that she was now genuinely in love with Mwinyi and asked Iddi not to bother her, as they were now planning their wedding. This letter tormented Iddi to the point where he did not know what to do, because he had already realized that all the plans he had made with Bahati were now ruined. However, the content of the letter was intended to test whether Iddi truly loved Bahati. Bahati knew that Iddi loved her because he became upset after reading the letter she had sent him. Mwinyi’s plans to gain wealth through Bahati had become nothing more than an unattainable dream. Suspense is another artistic technique that has been used to highlight social themes in Mohamed Suleiman's novel Kiu. This technique has been employed in the arrangement of plots and events, where right from the beginning the novel starts with suspense. The situation of delaying the reader from finding the solution to what is being described in the novel creates in the reader a desire to read more, as they will want to continue reading in order to reach the conclusion of the event. For example, at the beginning of the novel, it is described that Mwinyi lives in hardship and lacks happiness despite being a wealthy person. The thing that is said to be depriving Mwinyi of happiness is his love for Bahati, something he believes cannot succeed because he is an old man and Bahati is a young woman. discourses.translated_txt: In his novel *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman has used proverbs in his work as follows: Things were not good for Idi, as his intention was not to truly love her but merely to toy with her.

discourses.source_txt: Wazazi waliuo wengi wanafahamu kuwa, vijana wanapokuwa na mahusiano ya kimapenzi kabla ndoa mara nyingi huishia kuchezeana na suala la kuoana hupotea. Hivyo, kama mzazi Cheusi alimtaka binti yake aachane mara moja na Iddi.
discourses.translated_txt: Most responsible parents know that when young people engage in romantic relationships before marriage, it often leads to them toying with each other and the issue of marriage gets lost. Therefore, as a parent, Cheusi wanted her daughter to end things with Idi immediately.

discourses.source_txt: Msemo uliotumika katika kifungu hapo juu umetumika kujenga na kutoa msisitizo wa dhamira ya malezi ya mama kwa mto wake.
discourses.translated_txt: The proverb used in the above passage has been employed to build and emphasize the theme of a mother's guidance to her child.

discourses.source_txt: Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kuwa mazoe ni kitu kinachojenga tabia na daima mazoea huendelea daima (Ritzer, 2008).
discourses.translated_txt: Sociologists explain that habit is something that shapes character, and habits always persist (Ritzer, 2008).

discourses.source_txt: Kama katika jamii wasichana na wavulana wanaachwa huru kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa watalifanya hilo kuwa ni jambo sahihi na suala la kufunga ndoa halitakuwa na umuhimu kwao tena. discourses.translated_txt: If in society girls and boys are left free to have relationships before marriage, they will consider it acceptable, and the issue of getting married will no longer hold any significance for them. Parents must fulfill their responsibilities properly so that members of society, especially the youth, see that having relationships before marriage is a bad thing that should never be encouraged.

5.1.3 The Use of Metaphor in Kiu

A metaphor is a figure of speech that is used to compare two things with different characteristics without using any linking word of comparison, as is the case with simile (Kyando, 2013). The things being compared are considered to be entirely alike, without any differences.

discourses.source_txt: Kwa mfano, mtu anaweza akasema “Mwajuma ni sungura mdogo aliyejificha juu ya mti.” Hapa Mwajuma anafananishwa na sungura kana kwamba ni vitu viwili vilivyo sawa sawa bila ya tofauti hata kidogo.
discourses.translated_txt: For example, one might say, “Mwajuma is a little rabbit hiding in a tree.” Here, Mwajuma is being compared to a rabbit as if they are two things that are exactly alike, without any difference at all.

discourses.source_txt: Lengo hasa la kutumia sitiari katika kazi za fasihi ni kutoa msisitizo juu ya dhamira inayowasilishwa kwa msomaji.
discourses.translated_txt: The main purpose of using metaphors in literary works is to emphasize the theme being presented to the reader.

Mohamed Suleiman ametumia sitiari pale aliposema:
Watu waliposema kuwa hakuna aliyepata kumwia Mwinyi, maneno yao hayakuwa yametiwa chumvi. Mwinyi alikuwa na fedha za kutosha kujinunulia vingi ya vile mzee wa miaka sitini na miwili kama yeye angevitamani isipokuwa kitu kimoja tu.
discourses.translated_txt:
Mohamed Suleiman used a metaphor when he said:  
When people said that no one had ever outsmarted Mwinyi, their words were not exaggerated. Mwinyi had enough money to buy himself most of the things that a sixty-two-year-old man like him could desire, except for just one thing.

discourses.translated_txt: That is what made him feel as though his entire life had been wasted, and that his wealth was like a rice cake that had been spoiled with sand (p.01).

discourses.source_txt: Maneno yaliyokolezwa wino katika kifungu cha maneno hapo huu ni msemo unaoashira kuwa jambo au kitu kizuri sasa kimekuwa kibaya, kitu kitamu sasa kimekuwa kichungu na kitu cha thamani sasa thamani yake imepotea.
discourses.translated_txt: The words emphasized in ink in the phrase here express a saying that something good has now turned bad, something sweet has now become bitter, and something valuable has now lost its value.

discourses.source_txt: Mzee Mwinyi alikuwa ni tajiri mwenye kila aina ya mali lakini alitamani kuwa na mapenzi na binti aliyetokea kumpenda sana akiitwa Bahati. Kila mbinu aliyoitumia haikufanikiwa katika kumfanya Mwinyi ampate Bahati ndipo hata akalalamika kuwa, “utajiri wake mfano wa kitumbua kilichotiwa mchanga,” kwamba utajiri wake haumsaidii na wala hauna faida yoyote ile kwake.
discourses.translated_txt: Mr. Mwinyi was a wealthy man who possessed all kinds of riches, but he longed to have a romantic relationship with a young woman named Bahati, whom he had come to love deeply. Every approach he tried failed to win Bahati over, leading him to complain that “his wealth was like a cake mixed with sand,” meaning his wealth did not help him at all and was of no benefit to him.

discourses.source_txt: Kimsingi, kitumbua ambacho kinakuwa kimetiwa mchanga huwa hakiliki na ladha yake yote hupotea kwa sababu mlaji huogopa meno yake kutafuna mchanga.
discourses.translated_txt: Essentially, a rice cake that has sand mixed into it becomes inedible and loses all its flavor because the eater fears their teeth will bite into the sand.

discourses.source_txt: Msemo huu kwa hakika umetumika katika kutoa msisitizo wa dhamira ya mapenzi kuwa ikiwa mtu ni tajiri wa kila kitu lakini anapokosa mapenzi aliyoyatamani basi utajiri wake huwa si lolote na humfanya aishi kwa taabu na adha ya mawazo kiliko hata mtu maskini.
discourses.translated_txt: This saying has indeed been used to emphasize the theme of love—that if a person is wealthy in every material sense but lacks the love they long for, then their wealth becomes meaningless and causes them to live with more hardship and mental anguish than even a poor person.

discourses.source_txt: Wanasosholojia wanakiri kwamba vipo baadhi ya vitu ambavyo huonekana ni bora sana mtu kuwa navyo mathalani utajiri (Cross, 2011).
discourses.translated_txt: Sociologists acknowledge that there are certain things which are generally considered highly desirable to possess, such as wealth (Cross, 2011).

discourses.source_txt: Lakini hufika mahali mtu akakosa kitu ambacho alidhani kuwa ni kidogo na ule utajiri wake usimsaidie katika kukipata kitu hicho hali yeye aliamini kuwa utajiri wake ndio silaha ya kupata kila kitu.
discourses.translated_txt: However, there comes a time when a person lacks something they thought was minor, and their wealth does not help them obtain it, even though they believed their riches were the key to getting everything.

discourses.source_txt: Hii ni sawa na kusema kuwa, sasa kitumbua kimeingia mchanga kwani utajiri wote wa Mwinyi haukumwezesha kupata mapenzi ya Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: This is akin to saying that the rice cake now has sand in it, for all of Mwinyi’s wealth could not enable him to win Bahati’s love.

discourses.source_txt: Matumizi mengine ya msemo yanajitokeza pale ambapo Cheusi ambaye ni mama yake Bahati alipokuwa akimuonya mwanawe juu ya mahusiano yake na Iddi.
discourses.translated_txt: Another use of the saying appears when Cheusi, who is Bahati’s mother, was warning her daughter about her relationship with Idi.

discourses.translated_txt: Then Cheusi continued to advise her: "That Idi of yours, let me tell you, he doesn't want you, he has nothing.

discourses.translated_txt: Whoever truly desires a woman marries her. He just wants to toy with you and then discard you, moving on while laughing at you.

I have already realized that just because you have studied your English you think I am ignorant, well then … One day you will cry like a dog, mouth raised, and I will be here (pp. 25–26).” In this passage the writer uses the saying, “you will cry like a dog, mouth raised,” to refer to the theme of guidance and warnings given by a mother to her child. Cheusi was warning her daughter Bahati about the relationship she had started with
At that moment, Iddi, her driver, entered without knocking. Mwinyi was startled and asked him, “Why are you late?” Iddi wiped his sweat to show the effort he had made, shook his head sadly, and said, “I found the door locked.” Those words broke Mwinyi’s heart.

discourses.source_txt: Alishusha mabega akanywea juu ya kiti, akaona maisha yakimwonea.
discourses.translated_txt: He slumped his shoulders and shrank into the chair, feeling that life was being unfair to him.

discourses.source_txt: Kusubiri kusiko kikomo- miezi sita imepita na kutamani kusiko danganyika kukimtwesha. Alikuwa amekwishavumilia vya kutosha; bado hakujua ni lini siku ya faraja.
discourses.translated_txt: Waiting without end—six months had passed, and relentless yearning weighed heavily upon him. He had already endured enough; yet he still did not know when the day of relief would come.

discourses.source_txt: Lakini ah, maneno ya marehemu mama yake: Likufikalo patana nalo (uk.02).
discourses.translated_txt: But ah, her late mother’s words: “Whatever comes your way, accept it” (p. 02).

discourses.source_txt: Matumizi ya sitiari katika kifungu cha maneno hapo juu yanabainisha kuwa maneno yamefafanishwa na kisu au kitu chochote ambacho ni kikali chenye uwezo wa kukata kitu.
discourses.translated_txt: The use of metaphor in the above phrase shows that words are compared to a knife or anything sharp that is capable of cutting something.

discourses.source_txt: “Maneno yale yalimkata Mwinyi ini lake,” ni kauli yenye kuonesha kuwa matumaini ya Mwinyi kumpata Bahati yalikwishapotea mara baada ya taarifa kutoka kwa Iddi kuwa amemkosa Bahati na mlango wa nyumba ya Bahati umefungwa.
discourses.translated_txt: “Those words struck Mwinyi to the core,” is a statement that shows Mwinyi’s hope of winning Bahati had vanished as soon as he received information from Idi that he could not find Bahati and that Bahati’s door was locked.

discourses.source_txt: Wanasosholojia wanaeleza kuwa mwanadamu hufika mahali akakata tamaa juu ya kupata kitu fulani ambacho alitaraji kukipata kwa muda mrefu na asikipate (Webster, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Sociologists explain that a person may reach a point where they lose hope of obtaining something they have long desired but are unable to acquire (Webster, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: Kukata tamaa katika maisha ni jambo baya kwani huweza kumfanya mtu akafanya jambo baya ambalo hata linaweza kudhuru watu wengine. Kwa mfano, kitendo cha Mwinyi kukata tamaa ya kumpata Bahati kinaweza kikamfanya Mwinyi kuja na maamuzi ya kufanya uhalifu wa kubaka.
discourses.translated_txt: Losing hope in life is a bad thing because it can lead a person to do something harmful that may even endanger others. For example, Mwinyi's despair at not being able to have Bahati could drive him to make the decision to commit a crime such as rape.

discourses.source_txt: Kitendo cha ubakaji ni kibaya kwa ambaye atakuwa amebakwa lakini pia kwa mbakaji kwani huweza kuishia jela katika maisha yake yote yaliyobakia.
discourses.translated_txt: The act of rape is terrible for the victim but also for the perpetrator, as it can result in spending the rest of their life in prison.

discourses.source_txt: Mzee wa miaka sitini na miwili kama Mwinyi kufungwa jela ni kitu kibaya ambacho kinaweza kumfanya akafia huko jela.
discourses.translated_txt: For a sixty-two-year-old man like Mwinyi to be imprisoned is a terrible thing that could cause him to die in prison.

Personification is a figure of speech used to give balance and the ability to act like humans to creatures or objects that do not possess such abilities (Mlacha, 1989).

discourses.source_txt: Vitu kama vile miti, maneno, wadudu, wanyama na ndege wanaosawiriwa wakifanya vitendo vya kibinadamu hali ya kuwa hawana uwezo wa kufanya vitendo hivyo. Kwa mfano, si jambo la ajabu kuona katika fasihi ndege wakichumbiana na kupeleka posa la kuoa na hatimaye ndoa hufungwa na ndege hao wakaishi raha mustarehe (Senkoro, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Things such as trees, words, insects, animals, and birds are depicted as performing human actions even though they do not have the ability to do so. For example, it is not unusual in literature to find birds courting, proposing marriage, and eventually getting married and living happily ever after (Senkoro, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: Matumizi ya tashihisi katika kazi za fasihi hufanywa kwa lengo la kujenga dhamira kitaswira ili kumfanya msomaji atafakari kidogo ndipo aweze kupata dhamira iliyokusudiwa na mwandishi au msimuliaji wa kazi iliyo mbele yake.
discourses.translated_txt: The use of personification in literary works is intended to build the theme in an imaginative way so that the reader reflects a little in order to grasp the intended theme of the author or narrator of the work before them.

discourses.source_txt:
Katika riwaya ya Kiu kuna matumizi ya tashihisi yaliyotumiwa kwa lengo kama hilo ambayo yanajitokeza kama ifuatavyo:
“Ati watu husema mapenzi hayakutani, mbona yako wewe na Bahati yamekutana?”
Bahati alilia kwa kite na simanzi, hata usingizi ukamuonea huruma, ukamchukua hima na kumpumzisha kitandani.
discourses.translated_txt:
In the novel *Kiu*, there is the use of personification applied for this very purpose, as manifested in the following excerpt:
“People say that love never meets, but why have yours and Bahati’s?”
Bahati cried out with anguish and sorrow, until even sleep took pity on her, swiftly overtook her, and rested her on the bed.

discourses.source_txt: Alizindushwa na vishindo vya waenda msikitini, maana tayari kulikwisha pambazuka.
discourses.translated_txt: She was awakened by the clamoring of people going to the mosque, for dawn had already broken.

discourses.source_txt: Saa ya Bahati, siku zote ilikuwa wapiti njia. Alikuwa amekwishazoea kusikia wakati wa nyendo za wale waendao kazini, shule, misikitini, ndege za abiria, na waadhini (uk.20).
discourses.translated_txt: Bahati’s sense of time was always guided by passersby. She had become accustomed to hearing the movements of people going to work, to school, to the mosque, passenger airplanes, and the calls to prayer (p.20).

discourses.source_txt: Maneno yaliyokolezwa wino katika kifungu cha maneno hapo juu yametumiwa kitashihisi kwani katika maisha halisi ni mwanadamu pekee ndiye mwenye urari wa kuwa na huruma kwa mtu au kiumbe mwingine yoyote. Usingizi ni hali ya mtu kulala akawa hana fahamu kwani Waswahili husema, “usingizi ni nusu ya kufa.” Hata hivyo, katika kifungu cha maneno hapo juu inaonekana kuwa usingizi umepewa uwezo wa kuwa na huruma kama mwanadamu.
discourses.translated_txt: The words emphasized in the above passage are used as personification, because in real life only a human being is capable of showing compassion toward another person or creature. Sleep is a state in which a person loses consciousness, as expressed in the Swahili saying, "sleep is half of death." However, in the above passage, sleep appears to have been given the ability to feel compassion, as if it were human.

discourses.translated_txt:
5.1.5 The Use of Suspense in Kiu

Suspense is a literary technique used by authors of literary works to craft their works in such a way that they effectively convey their intended themes to the target audience.

discourses.source_txt: Hii ni mbinu ya kumchelewesha msomaji katika kupata suluhisho au ukweli wa mambo ulivyo na kumfanya aendelee kusoma zaidi mpaka pale atakapokutana na suluhisho au maelezo fulani yatakayompatia jawabu alilokusudia kulipata (Senkoro, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: This is a technique of delaying the reader from obtaining the solution or the truth of the matter, and making them continue reading until they encounter a solution or some explanation that will provide the answer they intended to find (Senkoro, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: Mbinu ya taharuki hutumiwa na watunzi wa kazi za fasihi kwa makusudi mazima ya kumpatia msomaji au msikilizaji hamu ya kusoma hasa kazi husika inapokuwa ni ndefu kiasi cha kumchosha msomaji. Urefu wa kazi utaonekana kuwa ni mfupi sana kama kutakuwa na taharuki zenye kumvutia msomaji.
discourses.translated_txt: The suspense technique is deliberately used by authors of literary works to give the reader or listener the desire to continue reading, especially when the work in question is lengthy enough to tire the reader. The length of the work will seem very short if there are suspenseful moments that captivate the reader.

discourses.source_txt:
Taharuki ni mbinu kongwe ya kifani inayotumika sana katika fasihi simulizi na hata katika fasihi andishi. Mohamed Suleiman katika riwaya yake ya Kiu ametumia mbinu hii kwa namna alivyoanza kusimulia hadithi yake. Kwa mfano:
Jioni hiyo alikuwa amejinyoosha juu ya kiti cha kulala, macho yake kayatupa darini, akihesabu dakika. Tamaa yake haikuwa kubwa, na wasiwasi wa kutofaulu ulimwondolea furaha. Lau kuwa alichokitaka kilikuwamo mikononi mwake, angekigugumia na kukata kiu yake.
discourses.translated_txt:
Suspense is an ancient literary technique that is widely used in oral literature and even in written literature. Mohamed Suleiman, in his novel *Kiu*, has employed this technique in the way he begins narrating his story. For example:

That evening, he was stretched out on a reclining chair, his eyes fixed on the ceiling, counting the minutes. His desire was not great, and the anxiety of failure had robbed him of joy. If only what he wanted was within his grasp, he would seize it and quench his thirst.

discourses.source_txt: Lau kuwa alichokitaka kingenunulika kwa fedha, bila shaka angezikwangua zote alizonazo.
discourses.translated_txt: If what he wanted could be bought with money, he would surely have scraped together every cent he had.

discourses.source_txt: Lakini kitu chenyewe kilikuwa ni hiari ya mtu mwingine, mwenye tadi na kiburi.
discourses.translated_txt: But the thing itself depended on the will of another person, someone with taste and pride.

discourses.source_txt: Kwa hivi alikuwa hana budi kuomba na kusubiri (uk.01-02).
discourses.translated_txt: So he had no choice but to ask and wait (pp. 01–02).

discourses.source_txt: Kifungu hiki cha maneno kina taharuki ndani yake ambapo kuna jambo linalomfanya Mwinyi kutokuwa na raha na kumtesa licha ya kuwa yeye ni tajiri.
discourses.translated_txt: This passage contains a sense of anxiety, as there is something that makes Mwinyi uncomfortable and torments him despite being wealthy.

discourses.source_txt:
Kitu hicho hakisemwi bayana bali inasemwa tu kama kupatikana kwa kitu hicho kulihitaji fedha basi Mwinyi angetoa
“Wacha masihara Iddi,” Mwinyi alimkaripia.
discourses.translated_txt:
This is not stated explicitly, but it is merely mentioned that if obtaining that thing required money, Mwinyi would provide it.  
“Stop joking, Iddi,” Mwinyi scolded him.

discourses.source_txt: “Unafikiri mtoto kama yule anaweza kumpenda mzee kama mimi (uk.05)?” Katika kifungu hiki taharuki iliyojengwa na mwandishi katika ukurasa wa kwanza wa riwaya yake inaanza kupata majawabu katika ukurasa wa tano.
discourses.translated_txt: “Do you think a child like that could love an old man like me (p.05)?” In this passage, the tension built by the author on the first page of his novel begins to find answers on page five.

discourses.source_txt: Hapo ndipo linapotajwa jambo linalomshughulisha Mwinyi kiasi cha kukosa raha pamoja na utajiri wake mkubwa alionao.
discourses.translated_txt: This is where the issue that troubles Mwinyi is mentioned, to the extent that he lacks peace despite all his great wealth.

discourses.source_txt: Kitu hicho si kingine bali ni mapenzi aliyokuwa nayo kwa binti aliyejulikana kwa jina la Bahati. Mwinyi alikuwa ni Mzee wa miaka sitini na miwili lakini alimpenda sana Bahati ambaye ni binti mdogo hata shule bado hajamaliza.
discourses.translated_txt: That thing is none other than the love he had for a girl known by the name Bahati. Mwinyi was a man of sixty-two years, but he loved Bahati very much, even though she was a young girl who had not yet finished school.

discourses.source_txt: Katika mazingira haya panajengeka tena taharuki nyingine ya kwamba Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa mpenzi wa Mzee mtu mzima kama alivyo Mwinyi? Hii nayo ni taharuki kwa wasomaji ambapo watavutiwa kusoma zaidi ili waweze kuona ni nini kitatokea juu ya mapenzi ya Mwinyi kwa binti Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: In this context, another tension arises: could Bahati agree to become the lover of an older man, just as Mwinyi did? This too creates suspense for the readers, who will be compelled to read further to find out what will happen regarding Mwinyi’s love for the young girl Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: Matumizi ya mbinu hii ya taharuki yametumiwa kwa lengo la kukuza na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi katika riwaya ya Kiu.
discourses.translated_txt: The use of this technique of suspense has been employed with the aim of enhancing and developing the theme of love in the novel Kiu.

discourses.source_txt: Mbinu hii inaonekana kutumiwa kwa mfululizo kwani pale jawabu au suluhisho la taharuki ya kwanza linapopatikana basi taharuki nyingine huibuliwa (Mlacha, 1991).
discourses.translated_txt: This technique appears to be used repeatedly, as whenever the answer or solution to the initial suspense is found, another suspense is introduced (Mlacha, 1991).

discourses.source_txt: Mathalani, katika kifungu cha maneno hapo juu tumepata suluhu kuwa jambo lilokuwa likimsumbua Mwinyi raha na kumkosesha usingizi ni mapenzi yake kwa binti Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: For example, in the excerpt above we find the solution that what had been troubling Mwinyi Raha and causing him sleepless nights was his love for Bahati's daughter.

discourses.source_txt: Baada ya kulijua hilo, imejengwa taharuki nyingine ya kuwa hivi binti mdogo kama Bahati anaweza kuridhia kuwa na mapenzi na Mzee Mwinyi ambaye anaweza kumtukuu Bahati?
discourses.translated_txt: After realizing this, another anxiety has arisen as to whether such a young girl like Bahati could agree to be in a relationship with old Mwinyi, who could even be Bahati's father.

discourses.source_txt: Wasomaji wataendelea kusoma zaidi mpaka pale watakapopata suluhisho na baada ya hapo watapata taharuki nyingine.
discourses.translated_txt: Readers will continue reading until they find a solution, and after that, they will encounter another anxiety.

discourses.source_txt: Hitimisho Lengo mahususi ya kazi hii ilikuwa ni kuchambua na kuelezea mbinu za kifani zilizotumika katika kujenga dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman. Hivyo, yaliyojiri ni pamoja na matumizi ya mbinu za kifani za barua, misemo, sitiari, tashihisi na taharuki.
discourses.translated_txt: Conclusion The specific objective of this work was to analyze and describe the stylistic techniques used to construct social themes in the novel "Kiu" by Mohamed Suleiman. Accordingly, the findings include the use of stylistic techniques such as letters, expressions, metaphors, personification, and anxiety.

discourses.source_txt: Matokeo ya utafiti yanaonyesha kuwa Riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman inasheheni utajiri mkubwa wa mbinu za kifani lakini katika utafiti huu tumeshughulikia vipengele vya matumizi ya mbinu ya barua, misemo, sitiari, tashihisi na taharuki tu. Sababu hasa ya kuteua mbinu hizi 5 ni kuwa zinatosheleza mahitaji ya malengo ya utafiti huu.
discourses.translated_txt: The research findings show that the novel 'Kiu' by Mohamed Suleiman is rich in stylistic techniques, but in this study we have focused only on the use of the letter-writing technique, sayings, metaphor, anxiety, and suspense. The main reason for selecting these five techniques is that they adequately meet the objectives of this research.

discourses.source_txt: Mbinu ya matumizi ya barua imetumiwa kwa lengo la kukuza na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi ambapo Bahati alitaka kujua kama Iddi anampenda kwa dhati. Bahati aliandika barua ya kumweleza Iddi kuwa sasa yeye bahati yupo katika mapenzi ya dhati na Mwinyi na anamuomba Iddi asimsumbue kwani hivi sasa wapo katika mipango ya harusi yao. Barua hiyo ilimtesa Iddi hata asijuwe ni jambo gani atafanya kwa sababu tayari alikwishafahamu kwamba mipango yote aliyoipanga yeye na Bahati sasa imekufa. Hata hivyo, yaliyosemwa katika barua hiyo yalilenga kumpima Iddi kama kweli anampenda Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: The use of the letter-writing technique was employed with the aim of developing and advancing the theme of love, in which Bahati wanted to know if Iddi truly loved her. Bahati wrote a letter to inform Iddi that she was now genuinely in love with Mwinyi and asked Iddi not to bother her, as they were now planning their wedding. This letter tormented Iddi to the point where he did not know what to do, because he had already realized that all the plans he had made with Bahati were now ruined. However, the content of the letter was intended to test whether Iddi truly loved Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: Bahati alifahamu kuwa Iddi anampenda kwa sababu alikasirika baada ya kuisoma barua aliyomtumia.
discourses.translated_txt: Bahati knew that Iddi loved her because he became upset after reading the letter she had sent him.

discourses.translated_txt: Mwinyi’s plans to gain wealth through Bahati had become nothing more than an unattainable dream.

discourses.source_txt: Taharuki ni mbinu nyingine ya kifani ambayo imetumika katika kuibua dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman. Mbinu hii imetumika katika upangaji wa visa na matukio ambapo mwanzo tu wa riwaya hii pameanza kitaharuki.
discourses.translated_txt: Suspense is another artistic technique that has been used to highlight social themes in Mohamed Suleiman's novel Kiu. This technique has been employed in the arrangement of plots and events, where right from the beginning the novel starts with suspense.

discourses.source_txt: Hali ya kumchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhisho la kile ambacho kinaelezwa katika riwaya kinamfanya msoamji kuwa na hamu ya kusoma zaidi kwani atataka kusoma zaidi ili apate mwisho wa tukio lake. Kwa mfano, mwanzoni mwa riwaya kunaelezwa kuwa Mwinyi anaishi kwa shida na kukosa raha licha ya kuwa yeye ni mtu tajiri.
discourses.translated_txt: The situation of delaying the reader from finding the solution to what is being described in the novel creates in the reader a desire to read more, as they will want to continue reading in order to reach the conclusion of the event. For example, at the beginning of the novel, it is described that Mwinyi lives in hardship and lacks happiness despite being a wealthy person.

discourses.source_txt: Jambo linaloezwa kuwa ndilo linalomnyima Mwinyi raha ni mapenzi yake kwa Bahati jambo ambalo aliona kuwa haliwezi kufanikiwa kutokana na yeye kuwa na ni Mzee na Bahati ni binti mdogo.
discourses.translated_txt: The thing that is said to be depriving Mwinyi of happiness is his love for Bahati, something he believes cannot succeed because he is an old man and Bahati is a young woman.

discourses.source_txt: Mbinu nyingine za kifani zilizotumika katika kujenga dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya Kiu ni misemo, sitiari na tashihisi. Mbinu hizi za kifani zimetumika katika kusisitiza masuala mbalimbali yanayohusiana na dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya Kiu.
discourses.translated_txt: Other stylistic techniques used to develop social themes in the novel "Kiu" include proverbs, metaphors, and personification. These literary techniques have been employed to emphasize various issues related to social themes in the novel "Kiu."
